newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar tumbles on commission selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar tumbles on commission selling.

text.p: London's December white sugar contract displayed continued weakness on its first day as spot position when a wave of commission house selling caused values to tumble, traders said on Monday.
"It's certainly looking weak," said one trader, adding that a fund might be behind at least some of the sales by a leading commission house.
One major trade house was also reported to have sold December positions, compounding the weakness.
At 1527 GMT December was down $5.50 at $333.00, after touching a low of $332.20, and the second-position March contract was down $3.30 at $333.50.
Volume was concentrated in the two front positions and totalled 1,714 lots.
In fundamental news, Egypt cancelled a tender for 25,000 tonnes of raw or white sugar, saying it received only one bid at $326 a tonne for raw sugar.
Trade sources said the sole bid was from Louis Dreyfus.
Elsewhere, a total of 281 lots of white sugar, equivalent to 14,050 tonnes, was delivered against the London October white sugar contract after it expired on Friday.
Refco was the deliverer of all the sugar from the Polish ports of Gdansk and Gdynia and the receivers were ICS and E D & F Man.
The trading pattern was similar in Paris, where all positions were lower. December was down $6.00 at $333.00 and March down $4.40 at $333.60.
